### Load packages and data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(glmnet)
library(here)
library(dplyr)


# Load the merged TPM dataset
analysis_tpm <- readRDS(here("data", "processed", "analysis_tpm.rds"))

# Check dimensions
dim(analysis_tpm)

```

### Separate the outcome and predictors

```{r}
# Outcome: Day 7 plasmablast frequency
y_vec <- analysis_tpm$plasmablast_frequency

# Identify gene columns using their Ensembl IDs
gene_cols <- grep(
  "^ENSG",
  names(analysis_tpm),
  value = TRUE
)

# Extract gene expression matrix
X_mat <- as.matrix(analysis_tpm[, gene_cols])

# Transform TPM values
X_mat <- log2(X_mat + 1)

# Verify dimensions
dim(X_mat)
length(y_vec)
```

We transform the TPM values using log2(TPM+1) because RNA-seq gene expression is typically highly skewed since many genes have low expression and only a small number have high expression.

The transformation compresses large values.

### Check the data

```{r}
# Confirm predictor and outcome dimensions match
stopifnot(nrow(X_mat)== length(y_vec))

# Check for missing values
sum(is.na(X_mat))
sum(is.na(y_vec))

# Check for infinite values
sum(!is.finite(X_mat))

# Summarize outcome
summary(y_vec)
```

### Explore outcome

```{r}
# Create histogram of the response

response_hist <- ggplot(
  analysis_tpm,
  aes(x = plasmablast_frequency)
) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 12) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Day 7 Plasmablast Frequency",
    x = "Day 7 plasmablast frequency",
    y = "Number of participants"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

response_hist
```

A bit right-skewed, keeping original scale for now, but we can try a transformation later as a sensitivity analysis.

### Check gene-expression variability

```{r}
# Calculate the variance of each gene across participants
gene_variances <- apply(X_mat, 2, var)

# Count genes with zero and nonzero variance
sum(gene_variances == 0)
sum(gene_variances > 0)

# Summarize gene variances
summary(gene_variances)
```

A substantial proportion of genes have no variation in expression across the 29 participants (25213) meaning these cannot help the elastic net model distinguish between individuals.

-   Total genes = 78,932

-   Zero-variance genes = 25,213 (31.9%)

-   Nonzero-variance genes = 53,719 (68.1%) (Genes whose expression differs between at least two participants)

Variance here is calculated after transforming expression values using log(TPM+1)

For the final predictive analysis we will have to perform gene filtering within the cross-validation training folds to avoid information leakage. Nonzero variance alone also does not mean that a gene is predictive of plasmablast frequency.

don't remove the 25,213 genes from the entire dataset yet. Instead, we filter genes separately within each training fold, so the held-out participants don't influence preprocessing

### Elastic net regression with nested cross-validation

```{r}

set.seed(123)
# Create five outer folds for model evaluation
folds <- createFolds(
  y_vec,
  k = 5,
  list = TRUE
)

# Check number of participants in each test fold
sapply(folds, length)
```

**Outer cross-validation:** Divides the 29 participants into five groups. Each group serves as the test set once, while the remaining participants are used for training.

**Inner cross-validation:** In each outer training set, we use another five-fold cross-validation procedure to select the optimal α and λ

#### Check gene filtering in one fold

```{r}
# Use the first outer fold as an example
test_idx <- folds[[1]]

# Split gene expression into training and testing sets
X_train <- X_mat[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
X_test  <- X_mat[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

# Split the outcome
y_train <- y_vec[-test_idx]
y_test  <- y_vec[test_idx]

# Identify genes with nonzero variance in training data
keep_genes <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

# Apply the SAME gene selection to both datasets
X_train <- X_train[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]
X_test  <- X_test[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]

# Check dimensions
dim(X_train)
dim(X_test)

# Number of genes retained
sum(keep_genes)
```

To evaluate elastic net predictive performance, five-fold outer cross-validation was used to separate training and testing participants. Within each training fold, genes with zero variance were removed, and the same gene subset was retained in the corresponding test set. This ensures that feature filtering is determined exclusively from training data. Elastic net hyperparameters α and λ will subsequently be tuned using five-fold inner cross-validation, with predictive performance evaluated on held-out participants.

### Fit elastic net using nested cross-validation

```{r}

# =========================================================
# Nested cross-validation: elastic net
# =========================================================

# Use the tuning grid and outer folds created previously.
# Replace the earlier lambda grid with values more appropriate
# for the small numerical scale of plasmablast frequency.

elastic_net_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
  lambda = c(
    0.000001,
    0.00001,
    0.0001,
    0.001,
    0.01,
    0.05,
    0.1
  )
)

# Create vectors for storing results
elastic_net_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))
baseline_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))

best_alphas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
best_lambdas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
genes_retained <- rep(NA_integer_, length(folds))

# Calculate RMSE only during inner cross-validation
rmse_only <- function(data, lev = NULL, model = NULL) {
  c(RMSE = sqrt(mean((data$obs - data$pred)^2)))
}

# Repeat across all five outer folds
for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

  cat("Running outer fold", i, "\n")

  # Select held-out participants
  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  # Divide data into training and testing sets
  X_train <- X_mat[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test  <- X_mat[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  y_train <- y_vec[-test_idx]

  # Identify genes with nonzero variance in training data
  keep_genes <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

  # Keep the same gene columns in training and testing sets
  X_train <- X_train[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_test[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]

  genes_retained[i] <- sum(keep_genes)

  # Inner cross-validation selects alpha and lambda
  elastic_net_model <- caret::train(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    method = "glmnet",
    tuneGrid = elastic_net_grid,
    trControl = trainControl(
      method = "cv",
      number = 5,
      summaryFunction = rmse_only
    ),
    metric = "RMSE",
    preProcess = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
    standardize = FALSE
  )

  # Predict participants in the held-out outer fold
  elastic_net_predictions[test_idx] <- as.numeric(
    predict(elastic_net_model, newdata = X_test)
  )

  # Simple reference model: training-set mean outcome
  baseline_predictions[test_idx] <- mean(y_train)

  # Store selected tuning parameters
  best_alphas[i] <- elastic_net_model$bestTune$alpha
  best_lambdas[i] <- elastic_net_model$bestTune$lambda
}

# Confirm all participants have a prediction
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(elastic_net_predictions),
  !anyNA(baseline_predictions)
)

```

#### Evaluate elastic net

```{r}

# RMSE: average magnitude of prediction errors
rmse_elastic_net <- sqrt(
  mean((y_vec - elastic_net_predictions)^2)
)

# Pooled cross-validated R-squared
r2_elastic_net <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - elastic_net_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# Compare with a simple baseline model
rmse_baseline <- sqrt(
  mean((y_vec - baseline_predictions)^2)
)

r2_baseline <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - baseline_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# Display results
data.frame(
  model = c("Elastic net", "Training-mean baseline"),
  RMSE = c(rmse_elastic_net, rmse_baseline),
  R2 = c(r2_elastic_net, r2_baseline)
)

# Inspect selected hyperparameters and retained genes
data.frame(
  fold = seq_along(folds),
  alpha = best_alphas,
  lambda = best_lambdas,
  genes_retained = genes_retained
)



```

RMSE = lower is better

baseline model is extremely simple. it doesn't use gene expression at all and just predicts the average plasmablast frequency of the training participants (just a simple average)

R^2^ = 1 is perfect prediction, R^2^ = 0 means predictions are as good as the overall sample mean, and R\^2 below 0 means predictions are worse than that overall-mean benchmark

-   **Small lambda:** The model is allowed to rely more strongly on gene expression patterns.

-   **Large lambda:** The model shrinks the gene coefficients more heavily, making its predictions less dependent on those patterns.

### plot observed versus predicted values

```{r}

library(ggplot2)

prediction_results <- data.frame(
  participant_id = analysis_tpm$participant_id,
  observed = y_vec,
  predicted = elastic_net_predictions
)

elastic_net_plot <- ggplot(
  prediction_results,
  aes(x = observed, y = predicted)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "Elastic Net: Observed vs Predicted",
    subtitle = "Five-fold nested cross-validation",
    x = "Observed Day 7 plasmablast frequency",
    y = "Predicted Day 7 plasmablast frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

elastic_net_plot

# Save figure
dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)

ggsave(
  "output/elastic_net_predictions.pdf",
  elastic_net_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 5
)

```

Elastic net regression was used to evaluate whether baseline gene expression could predict Day 7 plasmablast frequency. Five-fold nested cross-validation was implemented, with an inner loop for tuning the mixing parameter (α) and regularization strength (λ), and an outer loop for evaluating predictive performance in held-out participants. Genes with zero variance were removed using training data, and predictors were standardized within cross-validation. Predictive performance was evaluated using RMSE and cross-validated R² and compared with a training-mean baseline model.

### Additional analyses

#### Investigate prediction errors

plot shows that the model substantially underpredicts some participants with high plasmablast frequencies

identify those observations:

```{r}
# Calculate prediction errors for each participant
prediction_results <- prediction_results %>%
  mutate(
    error = predicted - observed,
    absolute_error = abs(error),
    squared_error = error^2
  )

# Participants with the largest prediction errors
prediction_results %>%
  arrange(desc(absolute_error)) %>%
  head(10)

```

check how much the largest errors contribute to overall performance:

```{r}
# Contribution of the three largest errors to total SSE
prediction_results %>%
  arrange(desc(squared_error)) %>%
  summarise(
    top_3_error_fraction =
      sum(head(squared_error, 3)) / sum(squared_error)
  )

```

**Just three of the 29 participants account for approximately 72% of the model's total squared prediction error.**

Prediction errors were examined to identify observations contributing disproportionately to overall model error. The three largest squared prediction errors accounted for 71.9% of the total sum of squared errors.

These observations corresponded to participants with relatively high Day 7 plasmablast frequencies (0.0341, 0.0280, and 0.0173), which were substantially underpredicted by the model. This suggests that the elastic net model had difficulty capturing higher plasmablast responses and tended to generate predictions closer to the population mean.

Given the small sample size, these observations substantially influenced model performance. However, they were retained in the analysis because high responses alone do not justify exclusion

### Compare with a demographic model

```{r}
# Prepare demographic data, including the outcome
clinical_data <- analysis_tpm %>%
  select(
    plasmablast_frequency,
    age,
    biological_sex
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    biological_sex = as.factor(biological_sex)
  )

# Check for missing values
colSums(is.na(clinical_data))

# Store held-out predictions
clinical_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))

# Use the SAME outer folds as elastic net
for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  # Separate training and testing participants
  clinical_train <- clinical_data[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  clinical_test <- clinical_data[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  # Fit regression using training participants only
  clinical_model <- lm(
    plasmablast_frequency ~ age + biological_sex,
    data = clinical_train
  )

  # Predict held-out participants
  clinical_predictions[test_idx] <- predict(
    clinical_model,
    newdata = clinical_test
  )
}

# Confirm predictions exist for all participants
stopifnot(!anyNA(clinical_predictions))

# Evaluate demographic model
rmse_clinical <- sqrt(
  mean((y_vec - clinical_predictions)^2)
)

r2_clinical <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - clinical_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# Compare models
data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Mean-only baseline",
    "Age + sex",
    "Elastic net gene expression"
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    rmse_baseline,
    rmse_clinical,
    rmse_elastic_net
  ),
  R2 = c(
    r2_baseline,
    r2_clinical,
    r2_elastic_net
  )
)

```

this will tell us if gene expression predicts the plasmablast response better than basic demographic information

**gene expression predicts Day 7 plasmablast frequency slightly better than age and sex alone**

### 

## Combined elastic net model with baseline gene expression + age + sex

```{r}

# =========================================================
# Combined elastic net: gene expression + demographics
# =========================================================

# Create numeric demographic predictors
# model.matrix() converts biological_sex into a dummy variable
demographic_mat <- model.matrix(
  ~ age + biological_sex,
  data = analysis_tpm
)[, -1, drop = FALSE]

# Combine gene expression with demographic predictors
X_combined <- cbind(
  X_mat,
  demographic_mat
)

# Check dimensions
dim(X_combined)

# Check demographic variable names
colnames(demographic_mat)

# Confirm rows match the outcome
stopifnot(
  nrow(X_combined) == length(y_vec),
  !anyNA(X_combined),
  all(is.finite(X_combined))
)

```

### Fit the combined elastic net

```{r}

# Store predictions for each participant
combined_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))

# Store the best tuning parameters
combined_alphas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
combined_lambdas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
combined_genes_retained <- rep(NA_integer_, length(folds))

# Reuse the SAME outer folds and tuning grid
for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

  cat("Running combined model - outer fold", i, "\n")

  # 1. Select held-out participants
  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  # 2. Split training and testing data
  X_train <- X_combined[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test  <- X_combined[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  y_train <- y_vec[-test_idx]

  # 3. Remove zero-variance predictors using training data
  keep_predictors <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

  X_train <- X_train[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]
  X_test  <- X_test[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]

  combined_genes_retained[i] <- sum(
    keep_predictors[seq_len(ncol(X_mat))]
  )

  # 4. Tune alpha and lambda using inner cross-validation
  combined_model <- caret::train(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    method = "glmnet",
    tuneGrid = elastic_net_grid,
    trControl = trainControl(
      method = "cv",
      number = 5,
      summaryFunction = rmse_only
    ),
    metric = "RMSE",
    preProcess = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
    standardize = FALSE
  )

  # 5. Predict held-out participants
  combined_predictions[test_idx] <- as.numeric(
    predict(combined_model, newdata = X_test)
  )

  # 6. Store selected parameters
  combined_alphas[i] <- combined_model$bestTune$alpha
  combined_lambdas[i] <- combined_model$bestTune$lambda
}

# Check that all 29 participants received predictions
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(combined_predictions),
  all(is.finite(combined_predictions))
)

```

### RMSE and R\^2

```{r}

# RMSE for combined model
rmse_combined <- sqrt(
  mean((y_vec - combined_predictions)^2)
)

# Cross-validated R-squared
r2_combined <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - combined_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# Compare all four models
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Mean-only baseline",
    "Age + sex",
    "Gene-expression elastic net",
    "Combined elastic net"
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    rmse_baseline,
    rmse_clinical,
    rmse_elastic_net,
    rmse_combined
  ),
  R2 = c(
    r2_baseline,
    r2_clinical,
    r2_elastic_net,
    r2_combined
  )
)

model_comparison

# Selected alpha and lambda in each outer fold
data.frame(
  fold = seq_along(folds),
  alpha = combined_alphas,
  lambda = combined_lambdas,
  genes_retained = combined_genes_retained
)


```

The gene-expression-only model performed best, although its advantage over the mean-only baseline was extremely small.

The combined model performed worse than both gene expression alone and the mean-only baseline.

### Sensitivity analysis: Log-transforming the outcome

```{r}
# Log-transform Day 7 plasmablast frequency
y_log <- log(y_vec)

# Compare distributions
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

hist(
  y_vec,
  main = "Original plasmablast frequency",
  xlab = "Day 7 plasmablast frequency"
)

hist(
  y_log,
  main = "Log-transformed frequency",
  xlab = "Log(Day 7 plasmablast frequency)"
)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

summary(y_log)
```

#### Fit the elastic net using this log-transformed outcome

```{r}
# Store predictions and selected hyperparameters
log_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))

log_alphas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
log_lambdas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
# Wider lambda grid for the log-transformed outcome
log_elastic_net_grid <- expand.grid(
  alpha = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
  lambda = c(
    0.000001,
    0.00001,
    0.0001,
    0.001,
    0.01,
    0.05,
    0.1,
    0.2,
    0.5,
    1
  )
)

for (i in seq_along(folds)) {
  cat("Running log-transformed model - outer fold", i, "\n")

  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  # Split expression data
  X_train <- X_mat[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_mat[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  # Use log-transformed outcome
  y_train <- y_log[-test_idx]

  # Remove zero-variance genes using training data only
  keep_genes <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

  X_train <- X_train[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_test[, keep_genes, drop = FALSE]

  # Fit elastic net with inner 5-fold CV
  log_model <- caret::train(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    method = "glmnet",
    tuneGrid = log_elastic_net_grid,
    trControl = trainControl(
      method = "cv",
      number = 5,
      summaryFunction = rmse_only
    ),
    metric = "RMSE",
    preProcess = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
    standardize = FALSE
  )

  # Predict on log scale and back-transform
  pred_log <- predict(log_model, newdata = X_test)

  log_predictions[test_idx] <- exp(pred_log)

  # Save selected parameters
  log_alphas[i] <- log_model$bestTune$alpha
  log_lambdas[i] <- log_model$bestTune$lambda
}
```

#### Compare predictive performance

```{r}
# Performance on original outcome scale
log_rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_vec - log_predictions)^2))

log_r2 <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - log_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# Compare models
data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Original outcome",
    "Log-transformed outcome"
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    sqrt(mean((y_vec - elastic_net_predictions)^2)),
    log_rmse
  ),
  R2 = c(
    1 - sum((y_vec - elastic_net_predictions)^2) /
      sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2),
    log_r2
  )
)

data.frame(
  Fold = seq_along(folds),
  Alpha = log_alphas,
  Lambda = log_lambdas
)
```

#### Visualize

```{r}
ggplot(
  data.frame(
    Observed = y_vec,
    Predicted = log_predictions
  ),
  aes(x = Observed, y = Predicted)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Elastic net with log-transformed outcome",
    x = "Observed Day 7 plasmablast frequency",
    y = "Predicted Day 7 plasmablast frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

#### Check individuals with high prediction error

```{r}
# Compare prediction errors between original and log-transformed models
error_comparison <- data.frame(
  participant_id = analysis_tpm$participant_id,
  observed = y_vec,
  original_predicted = elastic_net_predictions,
  log_predicted = log_predictions
) %>%
  mutate(
    original_squared_error = (observed - original_predicted)^2,
    log_squared_error = (observed - log_predicted)^2,
    original_error_percent = 100 * original_squared_error /
      sum(original_squared_error),
    log_error_percent = 100 * log_squared_error /
      sum(log_squared_error)
  )

# Show participants with the largest errors in the log model
error_comparison %>%
  arrange(desc(log_squared_error)) %>%
  select(
    participant_id,
    observed,
    original_error_percent,
    log_error_percent
  ) %>%
  head(10)

```

#### compare three largest errors

```{r}
# Identify the three largest errors in each model
top3_original <- error_comparison %>%
  slice_max(original_squared_error, n = 3)

top3_log <- error_comparison %>%
  slice_max(log_squared_error, n = 3)

# Compare their contributions
data.frame(
  Model = c("Original outcome", "Log-transformed outcome"),
  Top_3_Error_Percent = c(
    sum(top3_original$original_error_percent),
    sum(top3_log$log_error_percent)
  )
)

# Check whether they are the same participants
intersect(
  top3_original$participant_id,
  top3_log$participant_id
)
```

#### check the original 3 participants specifically

```{r}
# Contribution of the original top three participants
error_comparison %>%
  filter(participant_id %in% top3_original$participant_id) %>%
  select(
    participant_id,
    observed,
    original_error_percent,
    log_error_percent
  )

# Their combined contributions to each model
error_comparison %>%
  filter(participant_id %in% top3_original$participant_id) %>%
  summarise(
    Original_total_percent = sum(original_error_percent),
    Log_total_percent = sum(log_error_percent)
  )
```

## Add vaccine history

```{r}
# Load vaccination history
vaccine_hist <- readRDS(
  here("data", "vaccine_hist.rds")
)

# Identify participants with documented history
# The vaccine history dataset uses the subject identifier
vax_available <- analysis_tpm$subject %in% vaccine_hist$subject

# Check availability
table(vax_available)

# Examine vaccination counts among participants with records
summary(analysis_tpm$n_prior_vax[vax_available])

# Check the two participants without documented history
analysis_tpm %>%
  filter(!vax_available) %>%
  select(participant_id, subject, n_prior_vax)

```

#### create 27-participant dataset

```{r}
# Keep only participants with documented vaccination history
analysis_vax <- analysis_tpm[vax_available, ]

# Corresponding gene expression and outcome
X_vax <- X_mat[vax_available, , drop = FALSE]
y_vax <- y_vec[vax_available]

# Age and sex predictors
demographic_vax <- model.matrix(
  ~ age + biological_sex,
  data = analysis_vax
)[, -1, drop = FALSE]

# Age, sex, and vaccination history predictors
demographic_vax_history <- model.matrix(
  ~ age + biological_sex + n_prior_vax,
  data = analysis_vax
)[, -1, drop = FALSE]

# Create three predictor matrices
X_vax_gene <- X_vax

X_vax_demographic <- cbind(
  X_vax,
  demographic_vax
)

X_vax_full <- cbind(
  X_vax,
  demographic_vax_history
)

# Verify dimensions and missingness
dim(X_vax_gene)
dim(X_vax_demographic)
dim(X_vax_full)

stopifnot(
  length(y_vax) == 27,
  !anyNA(X_vax_full),
  !anyNA(y_vax)
)

```

#### Create outer cross validation folds

```{r}
set.seed(123)

folds_vax <- createFolds(
  y_vax,
  k = 5,
  list = TRUE
)

sapply(folds_vax, length)
```

#### fit the three models with vaccine history now (on the same 27 participants rather than 29)

```{r}
# Predictor matrices for the three models
vax_models <- list(
  "Gene expression" = X_vax_gene,
  "Genes + age + sex" = X_vax_demographic,
  "Genes + age + sex + vaccination history" = X_vax_full
)

# Store predictions for each model
vax_predictions <- list()

for (model_name in names(vax_models)) {

  cat("\nRunning model:", model_name, "\n")

  X_current <- vax_models[[model_name]]

  predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vax))

  for (i in seq_along(folds_vax)) {

    cat("Outer fold", i, "\n")

    test_idx <- folds_vax[[i]]

    X_train <- X_current[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
    X_test <- X_current[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

    y_train <- y_vax[-test_idx]

    # Remove zero-variance predictors using training data
    keep_predictors <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

    X_train <- X_train[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]
    X_test <- X_test[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]

    # Fit elastic net with inner cross-validation
    model <- caret::train(
      x = X_train,
      y = y_train,
      method = "glmnet",
      tuneGrid = elastic_net_grid,
      trControl = trainControl(
        method = "cv",
        number = 5,
        summaryFunction = rmse_only
      ),
      metric = "RMSE",
      preProcess = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
      standardize = FALSE
    )

    predictions[test_idx] <- as.numeric(
      predict(model, newdata = X_test)
    )
  }

  vax_predictions[[model_name]] <- predictions
}
```

#### compare performance

```{r}
# Training-mean predictions for the 27-participant cohort
vax_baseline_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vax))

for (i in seq_along(folds_vax)) {
  test_idx <- folds_vax[[i]]

  vax_baseline_predictions[test_idx] <- mean(y_vax[-test_idx])
}

# Calculate baseline performance
baseline_rmse_vax <- sqrt(
  mean((y_vax - vax_baseline_predictions)^2)
)

baseline_r2_vax <- 1 -
  sum((y_vax - vax_baseline_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vax - mean(y_vax))^2)

data.frame(
  Model = "Training-mean baseline (n = 27)",
  RMSE = baseline_rmse_vax,
  R2 = baseline_r2_vax
)

vax_results <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Training-mean baseline",
    names(vax_predictions)
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    baseline_rmse_vax,
    sapply(
      vax_predictions,
      function(p) sqrt(mean((y_vax - p)^2))
    )
  ),
  R2 = c(
    baseline_r2_vax,
    sapply(
      vax_predictions,
      function(p) {
        1 - sum((y_vax - p)^2) /
          sum((y_vax - mean(y_vax))^2)
      }
    )
  ),
  row.names = NULL
)

vax_results
```

### Try imputation instead of restriction (29 participants)

impute with population median

we'll calculate the vaccination-history median separately within each training fold to avoid information leakage

```{r}
# =========================================================
# Sensitivity analysis: Median imputation (n = 29)
# =========================================================

# Create vaccination history variable
# Missing history is represented by NA, not zero

vax_count <- analysis_tpm$n_prior_vax

vax_count[!vax_available] <- NA_real_

# Check missing values
sum(is.na(vax_count))

# Examine documented vaccination counts
summary(vax_count)
```

#### fit elastic net with training-fold median imputation

```{r}
# Store predictions and selected hyperparameters
vax_imputed_predictions <- rep(NA_real_, length(y_vec))

vax_imputed_alphas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))
vax_imputed_lambdas <- rep(NA_real_, length(folds))

for (i in seq_along(folds)) {

  cat("Running imputed vaccination model - fold", i, "\n")

  test_idx <- folds[[i]]

  # Separate training and testing data
  X_train <- X_combined[-test_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_combined[test_idx, , drop = FALSE]

  y_train <- y_vec[-test_idx]

  # Separate vaccination history
  vax_train <- vax_count[-test_idx]
  vax_test <- vax_count[test_idx]

  # Calculate median using training participants only
  training_median <- median(vax_train, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Impute missing vaccination histories
  vax_train[is.na(vax_train)] <- training_median
  vax_test[is.na(vax_test)] <- training_median

  # Add vaccination history to predictor matrices
  X_train <- cbind(X_train, n_prior_vax = vax_train)
  X_test <- cbind(X_test, n_prior_vax = vax_test)

  # Remove zero-variance predictors using training data
  keep_predictors <- apply(X_train, 2, var) > 0

  X_train <- X_train[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]
  X_test <- X_test[, keep_predictors, drop = FALSE]

  # Fit elastic net with inner cross-validation
  model <- caret::train(
    x = X_train,
    y = y_train,
    method = "glmnet",
    tuneGrid = elastic_net_grid,
    trControl = trainControl(
      method = "cv",
      number = 5,
      summaryFunction = rmse_only
    ),
    metric = "RMSE",
    preProcess = c("zv", "center", "scale"),
    standardize = FALSE
  )

  # Predict held-out participants
  vax_imputed_predictions[test_idx] <- as.numeric(
    predict(model, newdata = X_test)
  )

  # Store selected hyperparameters
  vax_imputed_alphas[i] <- model$bestTune$alpha
  vax_imputed_lambdas[i] <- model$bestTune$lambda
}

# Check predictions
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(vax_imputed_predictions),
  all(is.finite(vax_imputed_predictions))
)
```

#### compare results

```{r}
# Calculate performance
rmse_vax_imputed <- sqrt(
  mean((y_vec - vax_imputed_predictions)^2)
)

r2_vax_imputed <- 1 -
  sum((y_vec - vax_imputed_predictions)^2) /
  sum((y_vec - mean(y_vec))^2)

# Compare all models using the same 29 participants
imputation_results <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Training-mean baseline",
    "Genes + age + sex",
    "Genes + age + sex + imputed vaccination history"
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    rmse_baseline,
    rmse_combined,
    rmse_vax_imputed
  ),
  R2 = c(
    r2_baseline,
    r2_combined,
    r2_vax_imputed
  )
)

imputation_results
```

#### check selected hyperparameters

```{r}
data.frame(
  Fold = seq_along(folds),
  Alpha = vax_imputed_alphas,
  Lambda = vax_imputed_lambdas
)

```
